guidance: Ground truth for testing a prompt that outputs an age rating / classification and broadcast-time restrictions for UK and France, for LINEAR TELEVISION. On-demand and streaming are a different regime and are out of scope.
LONG format: one row per rule. The wide, per-category view is on the Pivot_Readable tab and is derived from these rows - edit here, not there.

content_category is the shared vocabulary. The content-extraction stage tags a scene with a content_category and the rule stage looks up rows with that category plus the relevant country and service_type. Keep the vocabulary closed; map each regulator's wording onto it rather than inventing new values.

Sort by authority_rank ascending; the lowest rank wins. Record the resolution in ambiguity_note. Worked example: C-01, where Arcom's own public summary page contradicted its binding text on the -12 hours and the binding text won.

determinacy describes THE RULE (is it a bright line or a judgment call?). ambiguity_flag describes OUR EXTRACTION (are we sure we read it right?). They are independent: a bright_line rule can be translation_uncertain, and a judgment_based rule can be perfectly clear. Merging them makes the test set unscoreable.

bright_line: exact match; any deviation is a defect. conditional: the correct answer, OR a correct missing-information request when the gating input was absent - both pass. judgment_based: score the cited rule and the reasoning, accept a band of outcomes, and require escalation near a threshold. Scoring a judgment_based row by exact match measures the test set, not the model.

Filter status = approved. Rows marked draft or unverified have open conflicts (see Open_Questions) and must be resolved first. Currently 74 of 83 rows are approved. The remaining: all FR category V rows are unverified (C-03), FR-CNV-001 is draft (channel conventions not collected, C-06), and FR-CLS-903 is a deliberately retained superseded row.

The biggest risk is that this table and the prompt share an author and therefore share mistakes - the exact failure Task 2 asks about. Mitigation: the bright-line rows (times, absolute prohibitions) should be INDEPENDENTLY RE-DERIVED from primary sources by a second pass that has not seen this table, then compared. verbatim_quote and source_url let a reviewer check a row without reading the prompt at all.
Never delete a row. When a source is replaced, set valid_to and status = superseded on the old row and add a new row. That preserves the ability to say which rule version produced a past decision.

country; service_type (free-to-air vs cinema channel vs pay-per-view vs premium subscription film); access measures in place (none / mandatory_daytime_protection / mandatory_restricted_access / decoder_lock); intended broadcast DATE and time (France has day-of-week and school-holiday rules); whether the asset is a theatrical film and its existing BBFC/CNC classification; whether it is a trailer or a music video. If any of these is missing and a candidate rule depends on it, the correct output is a missing-information flag, NOT an assumption.

Absolute prohibitions should be enforced in CODE, not left to prompt reasoning: UK-GEN-001 (seriously impair), UK-SEX-001 (R18-equivalent), UK-FLM-001 (refused classification), UK-FLM-006 (R18 films), FR-LAW-001 (nuire gravement), FR-PRO-001/002/003 (human dignity, child pornography, extreme violence). No contextual argument or access measure should be able to override these.
